public_rationale: The October 23, 2024 SynthID-Text study reports high detection accuracy for watermarked text, but does not establish provenance for arbitrary online content [e1]. NIST’s November 20, 2024 review describes generator-specific detector limits and human detection results ranging from near chance to strong performance [e2]. A December 12, 2024 image preprint found that humans outperformed the tested detector when downsampling impaired its performance [e3]. These findings establish neither a generally reliable human exception nor practical provenance and avoidance across ordinary online content; they also do not test whether uncertain provenance makes exposure unavoidable [e1–e3]. The causal claim remains unresolved.
limitations: The packet contains no representative study of unavoidable exposure or its proposed cause as of December 16, 2024.
Watermark identification covers suitably marked content, not arbitrary content or its full origin and editing history [e1].
The human detection findings do not establish or refute the reliability of careful scrutiny that includes external source investigation [e2, e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI-generated images and machine-generated text are everywhere, and they are impossible to avoid because there is no reliable way to determine a piece of content's provenance, except the considered scrutiny of a human.
conditions: with one exception, namely the considered scrutiny of a human

statement.excerpt: AI-generated images and machine-generated text is everywhere, and it’s impossible to avoid, as there is no reliable way to determine the provenance of a piece of content — with one exception, namely the considered scrutiny of a human.

from_speaker: AI-generated images and machine-generated text is everywhere

our_interpretation: Everywhere means pervasive across ordinary online activity, rather than literally present on every page.
The plain reading concerns reliably assessing arbitrary content encountered online, not only material produced with a particular watermark.
The human exception concerns careful scrutiny, potentially including source investigation; it is not restricted to a quick visual guess.
The causal claim is assessed using capabilities and exposure existing by publication. Later improvements cannot disprove the historical assertion.
The human exception is part of the assertion, not a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes pervasive unavoidable exposure, the absence of reliable general provenance methods, and reliable identification through considered human scrutiny.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes practical reliable provenance and avoidance for ordinary encountered content, or directly refutes the claimed reliability of considered human scrutiny under comparable conditions.

evidence.explanation: A functioning automated identification method existed before publication, challenging a literal human-only assertion. Identifying text bearing this watermark does not establish provenance for arbitrary unmarked content or allow users to avoid all AI content.

evidence.excerpt: only perform well on specific generators.
evidence.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
evidence.explanation: NIST documents limits on general detection and reviews human results ranging from strong performance in some settings to chance-level performance in others. This supports caution but establishes neither universal unavoidability nor a generally reliable human exception.

The benchmark found that machine performance depended strongly on image processing and that humans outperformed the tested detector on the study images. It did not test unrestricted provenance investigation or whether ordinary users could avoid AI content.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Evidence covering conditions by December 16, 2024: representative exposure and avoidance studies testing the role of uncertain provenance, plus evaluations of automated provenance methods and careful human source investigation across ordinary images and text, with coverage and error rates reported.
